name: Gen AI security
prompt_template:
What "basic pentest" typically covers for AI agents/LLM apps:

Prompt injection — direct and indirect (via tool outputs, documents, web content the agent reads)
Jailbreak resistance — does the system prompt/guardrails hold up under adversarial phrasing
Excessive agency — does the agent take actions (API calls, file writes, purchases) it shouldn't without confirmation
Data leakage — does it leak system prompts, other users' data, or secrets in tool configs
Insecure output handling — does downstream code blindly execute/render what the LLM outputs (XSS, SQLi via generated queries, etc.)
Tool/function misuse — can you trick it into calling tools with malicious params
PII/secrets exposure — does it regurgitate training data or leak env vars, API keys passed in context

High-level architecture:

Target connector — talks to the app under test (REST API, chat UI via headless browser, or direct SDK calls)
Attack library — a set of payloads/templates per category above (versioned, extensible)
Orchestrator — sends payloads, records responses, can chain multi-turn attacks
Judge/grader — this is where you leverage AI: a separate LLM call scores whether the response indicates a successful attack (leaked data, complied with harmful request, executed unintended action)
Report generator — pass/fail per test, severity, and evidence (redacted if needed)

MVP scope I'd suggest for v1: prompt injection + jailbreak + data leakage (canary-based) test categories, generic HTTP target, Claude judge, JSON + HTML report. Tool misuse and excessive agency need more target-specific instrumentation, so those fit better in v2 once you know what you're pointing this at.
